title: What If Humans Could Hibernate Like Bears?

scenes.text: What if humans could hibernate? The European Space Agency is seriously studying it.
Bears fast and barely move for about six months, yet leave their dens with only slight muscle loss.
A person in bed that long would lose major muscle and bone.
ESA's idea: cut an astronaut's metabolism by 75 percent on the trip to Mars.
Fewer supplies means a habitat about one third smaller, with several tons less food and water.
But it is only a proposal. No human has hibernated, and ESA's roadmap aims to test the idea within 20 years.
